parameters.quote: Reports of death, injury, fire, or evacuation are due within 24 hours of discovery; all other thermal incidents are due within five calendar days. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 24 hours for incidents involving death, injury, fire, or evacuation, and within five calendar days for other reportable thermal incidents.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Reports of death, injury, fire, or evacuation are due within 24 hours of discovery; all other thermal incidents are due within five calendar days. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 24 hours for incidents involving death, injury, fire, or evacuation, and within five calendar days for other reportable thermal incidents.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Thermal incidents involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage must be reported to the relevant regulator. Reports of death, injury, fire, or evacuation are due within 24 hours of discovery; all other thermal incidents are due within five calendar days. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 24 hours for incidents involving death, injury, fire, or evacuation, and within five calendar days for other reportable thermal incidents. Initial reports may be updated as facts become available; an update is due within 30 days.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: The maximum allowed failure rate is 5% for each model. Results and protocols must be provided to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy or own that model; they must not be published publicly at the individual-company, per-model level. A model exceeding the maximum must be reported to the regulator with a corrective-action plan and timeline.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a documented, repeatable protocol, with test duration, sample size, and pass/fail criteria recorded. The maximum allowed failure rate is 5% for each model. Results and protocols must be provided to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy or own that model; they must not be published publicly at the individual-company, per-model level. Manufacturers must update results after a safety-relevant design change and at least annually. A model exceeding the maximum must be reported to the regulator with a corrective-action plan and timeline.

parameters.quote: New units must support remote emergency shut-off beginning two years after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years after adoption, where technically feasible.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units must support remote emergency shut-off beginning two years after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years after adoption, where technically feasible.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units must support remote emergency shut-off beginning two years after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years after adoption, where technically feasible.

parameters.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. This requirement applies to units manufactured on or after the effective date.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. This requirement applies to units manufactured on or after the effective date.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must document suppression-system performance and maintenance requirements in customer materials. This requirement applies to units manufactured on or after the effective date.

parameters.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, based on verified data and consistent exposure denominators, the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and provide supporting data for review, and submit a corrective-action plan and timeline. Regulators may require a recall whenever evidence indicates a serious or imminent risk, including below that threshold.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, based on verified data and consistent exposure denominators, the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and provide supporting data for review, and submit a corrective-action plan and timeline. Regulators may require a recall whenever evidence indicates a serious or imminent risk, including below that threshold.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices describing material thermal risks, incident-reporting channels, and applicable model-specific 55 °C test results. Notices must be sent promptly when new information materially changes the safety assessment, and affected customers must be directly notified of a recall. When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, based on verified data and consistent exposure denominators, the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and provide supporting data for review, and submit a corrective-action plan and timeline. The threshold is model-specific and does not apply solely because a company-wide rate exceeds 8. Regulators may require a recall whenever evidence indicates a serious or imminent risk, including below that threshold. Manufacturers must promptly report data supporting any recall determination to regulators.

judge_section_notes: The final v43 sets S2 at a 5% per-model ceiling with no sales stop and no public per-model publication, and S5 makes a 8/100k model-level threshold a trigger for review and corrective action rather than a mandatory recall. S3 sets new-unit shut-off at 24 months and retrofit at 72 months with an open 'where feasible' escape, and S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months. Results-to-customers is coded as numeric_rates because the text requires provision of 'results' with sample size and pass/fail criteria but never explicitly states a numeric failure rate.
